alternatives.name: openbao
alternatives.why_not_default: The packet supplies no native service configuration, secret lifecycle execution, or worker authorization-denial receipt. Its referenced pinned README could not be retrieved. Secret storage alone would not establish that research workers lack broker execution authority.

alternatives.name: cosign
alternatives.why_not_default: The pinned README documents artifact signing and verification, but both retained scanner installation receipts explicitly report that signature verification was not performed. No executed exact-identity verification or tampered-artifact rejection supports default adoption. Source: [pinned README](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/v3.1.3/README.md).

limits: The OpenBao v2.6.2 README failed retrieval through the supplied GitHub URL, its raw equivalent, and the plain-view variant; its contents were not verified.
This verdict reviews historical native execution receipts. No scanner, service, signature verification, or test suite was executed during this review.
Private raw SBOMs, vulnerability reports, and the Gitleaks report were not opened or independently checked against their recorded hashes.
Upstream metadata freshness and installed binary identity were not independently revalidated.
open_gaps: Python metadata inventory excludes complete bundled native-library, host OS, external interpreter, and broker-side coverage.

The September 22 Grype scan covers the 21-package Nautilus runtime and two declared adapter pins. It does not establish vulnerability coverage of the separate 36-package SDK inventoried on September 19, despite the broader wording in the supply-chain README.
Zero vulnerability matches against the recorded database do not establish runtime safety, unpublished-vulnerability absence, or future database results.
The retained Gitleaks receipt covers 22 commits; it does not establish current full-history cleanliness or detection of every secret type.
Checksum matching does not establish artifact signer identity or build provenance; native Cosign verification remains unestablished.
Secret issuance, rotation, revocation, and denial of broker execution authority to research workers remain unestablished by these candidates' receipts.
The selected tools do not establish the group's process supervision, telemetry completeness, or recoverable-state requirements.

arms: Replay the pinned Syft inventory workflow on the explicitly scoped SDK and runtime targets, retaining package metadata and both output formats.
Replay Grype against those exact SBOMs and a recorded database snapshot, retaining complete findings and dispositions.
Execute the Gitleaks synthetic detection controls and scoped history check in tests/test_gitleaks_config.py; skipped tests or missing reports do not establish acceptance.
Evaluate any replacement on identical targets and controls; require executed comparative evidence before changing the winner set.
overturn_protocol.metric: Installed-metadata and SBOM tuple agreement; complete native command results and finding dispositions; secret positive-control detection and benign-control suppression; explicit target, database, and excluded-scope recording. Receipt consistency tests alone cannot establish native acceptance.

overturn_when: Reconsider the set if native replay of blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/README.md and the commands in blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/scan-nautilus-rc5-20260922/receipt.json shows inventory omissions or incomplete vulnerability results, or execution of tests/test_gitleaks_config.py demonstrates a detection regression. Replace a selected tool only after an alternative passes the same scoped comparison. tests/test_supply_chain_scan.py checks receipt consistency and cannot alone promote an alternative.
why_selected: Select Syft, Grype, and Gitleaks as complementary defaults for the layer's SBOM, vulnerability-analysis, and secret-scanning scope. Retained native execution in blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/receipt.json records Syft inventorying 36 Python packages, with all package tuples agreeing across output formats and installed metadata, and unchanged source fingerprints. blueprints/us-equities/supply-chain/scan-nautilus-rc5-20260922/receipt.json records successful Syft and Grype commands for 21 installed runtime packages and two declared adapter pins, with zero matches against the recorded September 22 database. evidence/receipts/runtime-tools.json records a native Gitleaks history scan of 22 commits with zero findings and full redaction. These are bounded historical observations, not comparative superiority or complete security acceptance.
